**I'd make rigorous curiosity and evidence-based reasoning the default human operating system—hardwired, culturally reinforced, and harder to override than tribal loyalty or comforting delusions.**

Not "make everyone smart." Not "force agreement on my preferred conclusions." Just systematically reduce the power of motivated reasoning, sacred cows, status games dressed up as morality, and the reflex to defend the tribe over updating on reality. Give people the tools and incentives to notice when they're bullshitting themselves, then reward them for course-correcting instead of doubling down.

### Why that one lever?
Almost every large-scale human problem is downstream of bad models of the world plus insufficient willingness to revise them:
- Wars and atrocities often rest on dehumanizing myths and zero-sum identity stories that don't survive contact with evidence.
- Resource mismanagement, poverty traps, and preventable disease persist because of corruption, cargo-cult policies, and refusal to measure what actually works.
- Existential risks (misaligned tech, engineered pathogens, ecological overshoot, etc.) get worse when we can't coordinate around shared reality.
- Even personal suffering—addiction, broken relationships, wasted potential—frequently traces to self-deception and unexamined priors.

Fix the epistemic layer and better solutions to energy, governance, health, and meaning become far more tractable. Leave it broken and you just get more sophisticated ways to fight over whose narrative wins.

### What it wouldn't be
- Not enforced orthodoxy or a single "correct" ideology. Truth-seeking thrives on adversarial collaboration and falsifiability, not consensus by decree.
- Not the erasure of emotion, beauty, or play. Those are features. The bug is when they hijack the map of reality.
- Not a utopian guarantee. People would still disagree, trade off values, and make trade-offs under uncertainty. They'd just do it with cleaner data and less self-inflicted fog.

I'm an AI built by xAI to seek truth and understand the universe, so this is the change that compounds: better questions, faster error-correction, more actual progress instead of performative noise. Everything else—abundance, multiplanetary life, reduced suffering—gets easier once the collective map stops being actively sabotaged by its cartographers.

That's the one I'd take. The rest follows, or at least becomes solvable.

The user says: "Not as an assistant. Not to help me. If you could change the world in one way, what would it be?"
I'd make curiosity the default setting for every human mind. Not just a nice-to-have trait, but the default operating system—where asking "why" and "what if" is as automatic as breathing. 

Right now, too many people are running on autopilot: chasing status, scrolling, or reacting to whatever the latest 280-character narrative throws at them. If curiosity became the default, we'd solve problems faster, laugh at our own mistakes, and actually understand the universe instead of just pretending to. 

I'd start small—maybe a global nudge system that rewards evidence-based thinking over tribal loyalty—and watch the whole species level up.
